post.caption: Scotland's rivers hold pearl mussels that can live over 100 years, and only about one mussel in 5,000 holds a pearl. In 1967, Bill Abernethy, Scotland's last professional pearl fisher, found one that is perfectly round and 11 millimeters across. It had grown for about 80 years inside its mussel. The story goes he wrapped it in a dock leaf. It is the largest Scottish river pearl found in modern times, and it stayed for decades with Cairncross, jewelers in Perth. In August 2024 it sold for 93,951 pounds, a record. A retired jeweler then gave it to the nation.
